beats.spoken: Who actually decides how your cream gets made?
Article 8 of the EU cosmetics regulation requires cosmetics to be made in line with good manufacturing practice. The aim is a high level of protection for human health.

How to do it is set out in a standard: ISO 22716. It gives guidelines for production, control, storage and shipment. If a maker follows the relevant harmonised standards, good manufacturing practice is presumed.

But the standard has limits. It covers product quality, not worker safety in the plant and not environmental protection. Research and development, and the distribution of finished products, aren't covered either.

Every product's information file includes a description of the manufacturing method and a statement that good manufacturing practice is followed. Even traces of banned substances are only allowed if they're technically unavoidable under good manufacturing practice.
For you, that means: the batch number on the pack links your product to exactly this manufacturing run. Note it down if you ever want to report a problem.
Read the batch first, then apply. Beauty knowledge, clearly explained: follow Dewlane.
